To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the drag-reducing ability of PEO is enhanced by binding of cationic surfacetant micelles, and that the drag reduction efficiency of the polymer-surfactant mixture is determined by the relative amounts of polymer and bound surfactant.
the critical PEO MW for drag reduction is lowered by the presence of HTAC and that the optimum PEO MW for maximum drag reduction increases as the HTAC concentration is increased.

drag reduction is observed for aqueous PEO solutions above the critical molecular weight and that the critical molecular weight decreases and maximum drag reduction increases in the presence of HTAC micelle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of surfactant binding on polymer-surfactant interaction and the effect on drag reduction in turbulent Couette flow.
polymer-surfactant interactions in aqueous solutions and the effect of these interactions on drag reduction.
the effects of surfactant on drag reduction and polymer-surfactant interactions in aqueous solutions of nonionic PEO and cationic HTAC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drag reduction is a function of the polymer concentration, the surfactant concentration, the molecular weight, and a surfactant-polymer interaction parameter.
the polymer-surfactant complexes formed in the present study have a significant effect on turbulent drag reduction.
polymer-surfactant interactions in aqueous solution result in an increase in hydrodynamically effective molecular weight and an increase in hydrophobicity, both of which contribute to drag reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
drag reduction is achieved by the formation of a polymer-surfactant surface complex that reduces the effective viscosity at the wall.
the optimum PEO molecular weight and concentration for drag reduction decreases in the presence of HTAC, and that the % maximum drag increases with HTAC concentration.

for a fixed HTAC/PEOMBC ratio, the optimum PEOF concentration for maximum drag reduction is the same as the critical concentration, c(POE)*, for drag reduction in the absence of surfactant, and this optimum PEO concentration scales inversely with the molecular weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the drag reduction efficiency of PEO is significantly enhanced by the binding of HTAC to PEO, and this is consistent with the interpretation that drag reduction is due to the formation of a polymer-surfactant (PS) complex.
drag reduction is observed for PEO/HTAC mixtures at lower PEO molecular weight, and higher concentration than in the absence of surfactant.
polymer-surfactant interactions are important in determining the drag reduction properties of polymer-surfactants mixtures.
